routes.label: Find the angle sum in two ways

question: The measures of the interior angles of a convex polygon are in arithmetic progression. If the smallest angle is \(100^\circ\) and the largest angle is \(140^\circ,\) then the number of sides the polygon has is
solution:
The endpoints of an arithmetic progression determine its average, even when the number of terms is unknown. Let \(n\geq 3\) be the number of sides and let \(S\) be the sum of the interior angles. Writing the progression forwards and backwards pairs each angle with one whose sum with it is \(100^\circ+140^\circ=240^\circ\). Thus
\[
S=\frac{n(100^\circ+140^\circ)}{2}
=120^\circ n.
\]
A convex \(n\)-gon can be divided into \(n-2\) triangles by diagonals from one vertex, so its interior-angle sum is also \(180^\circ(n-2)\). Equating the two expressions and canceling the degree unit gives
\[
120n=180(n-2),\qquad 60n=360,
\]
so \(n=6\). The polygon has \(\boxed{6}\) sides, choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
